results.title: OptST: Optimizing Semantic Tokenization for LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
results.content:
We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different [...] We study how pretrained hierarchical semantic tokenizers can be adapted for downstream recommendation. We frame this adaptation around two complementary dimensions: the codebook geometry should make token assignments responsive to recommendation signals, while the quantization depth should provide an appropriate semantic resolution for each user–item interaction.

We propose OptST, which keeps the pretrained semantic encoder and base codebooks frozen while adapting the effective RQ geometry through shared low-rank transformations, anchor regularization, and straight-through token assignment. An interaction-conditioned depth selector provides complementary control over the resolution exposed to the downstream recommender. [...] The first challenge is to make the assignment geometry responsive to downstream recommendation supervision while constraining its deviation from the pretrained geometry. OptST constructs each effective codebook through a near-identity low-rank transformation of its frozen base codebook. It retains hard nearest-code assignment in the forward pass and uses a soft relaxation to propagate recommendation gradients in the backward pass. An anchor regularizer further constrains the resulting geometric deformation.
